purpose: Stable IDs for rules so policy can be changed without rewriting evidence or canon data.

rules.text: Losing/obsolete evidence is preserved; runtime eligibility is separate from archival preservation.
Newer timestamp/version is not scientific evidence by itself.
Scientific/technical claims are compared only after normalizing configuration, load, date, environment and definition.
A fatal physical inconsistency blocks runtime use until repaired even if a document is newer.
Invention, test, adoption, production, training and unit-median clocks remain separate.
Downstream battle outcomes cannot prove upstream technical capability except through an explicit learning/feedback edge.
A bounded/provisional value is carried as a band; it is not silently replaced by historical baseline.
Effects entering the same intermediate state are integrated there once; do not multiply duplicate representations.
Effects at distinct causal stages may compound; threshold and resource-reallocation effects must be checked.
Each mandatory event domain must resolve ACTIVE, NO_RELEVANT_DELTA, NOT_YET_MATURE, or UNKNOWN before execution.
Changing a checkpoint invalidates descendants, not ancestors or independent siblings.
Changing PREWAR/WARSTART runtime canon creates a new baseline; descendants require impact revalidation or rerun.
A citation/evidence-pointer correction that leaves runtime value unchanged does not invalidate descendants.
Rule changes occur through explicit override records keyed by rule ID; old rule versions remain preserved.
